title: Roadmap Sync Fabric: Commitment Windows & Remediation Playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, deterministic mechanism (the 'Roadmap Sync Fabric') to capture cross-team commitment windows, automated readiness checks, and an operational remediation playbook so PM/Eng/Design/Security/Infra can make fast, traceable decisions when roadmap dependencies shift.

Scope:
- Specification of commitment windows (a configurable timeframe per initiative where downstream teams must signal readiness or flag risks).
- A small Console dashboard widget that surfaces outstanding commitments and automatic escalation status.
- A notifications/handshake protocol: each dependency owner gets a single canonical ask (Ready / At-Risk / Blocked) with a short rationale field and optional links.
- Remediation playbook templates for common failure modes (e.g., infra capacity shortfall, design blocker, security gating).
- Integration points for Linear (tickets created/linked), Slack escalation channel, and a Confluence template.

Out of scope for this ticket (will be follow-ups): deep automation to remediate infra (auto-scale actions), formal SLA enforcement, and full RBAC flows for enterprise tenants.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Product spec doc in Confluence exists and is reviewed by Eng, Design, Security, and Infra (links below).
2) Console prototype widget implemented behind a feature flag showing a list of commitments for a single initiative and status (Ready/At-Risk/Blocked) updated by owners.
3) Linear integration: when a commitment becomes At-Risk/Blocked, a standardized Linear sub-issue is created and linked to the owning initiative.
4) A remediation playbook (markdown) with at least three templates is stored in Confluence and linked from the widget.
5) Run a cross-team tabletop (30m) with a sample initiative and collect feedback; record action items.
6) Success metrics defined (time-to-resolution, % commitments updated within window, number of escalations avoided) and a monitoring dashboard populated with initial data.

Proposed solution summary:
- Short-form commitment model: owner, due-window (start/end), ask (Ready/At-Risk/Blocked), rationale, optional link to artifact.
- Console widget pulls commitments from a lightweight commitments service (API) and allows owners to update status inline.
- Commitments service emits events to a small orchestration lambda that creates Linear tickets and posts to an escalation Slack channel.
- Playbook stored in Confluence; widget includes direct links to the appropriate playbook template for the selected failure mode.

Trade-offs considered:
- Minimal UI vs. heavy process: chose minimal to reduce friction; may need later UX polish.
- Centralized service vs. per-project hooks: centralized service simpler for analytics, but requires operational ownership (ops burden).
- Auto-remediation vs. human-in-the-loop: start human-first to avoid surprising production actions.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Ava Martinez (owner), Product Analytics: Jonah Reed, Eng: Ravi Patel (backend lead), Design: Mei Chen, Security: Priya Kapoor, Infra: Lucas Nguyen, DevRel: Sofia Ortiz.

Links and artifacts: 
- Confluence spec (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RD/Roadmap+Sync+Fabric+Spec (draft)
- Console prototype Figma frames: https://drive.redwood.ai/figma/roadmap-sync-fabric (perm restricted)
- Linear integration PR (server): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2187 (WIP)
- Playbook templates (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RD/Remediation+Playbooks

Rollout plan:
1) Ship behind feature flag to three internal initiatives for Q2 trial.
2) Iterate on ask phrasing and widget UX based on tabletop feedback.
3) Expand to all initiatives once % commitments updated within window > 75% and mean time-to-resolution drops by 20%.

Monitoring and success metrics:
- Time-to-resolution for At-Risk/Blocked commitments (target: < 72 hours first pass).
- Commitment update rate within a window (target: >= 75%).
- Number of escalations routed to Ops per initiative (target: reduce by 30% after 1 quarter).

Security review required: yes (security signals and playbook templates include guidance for sensitive data).

Customer impact: medium (internal roadmap reliability improves release predictability; external customers see downstream benefit through fewer slip-driven incidents).
